# ISSUE-284 plan

Support personal and organization-owned contributor forks through one shared verifier, preserving the upstream coordinator's authority and fenced publication. Planning only; no production changes or GitHub mutations.

## Dimensions

Approved: multi_area / known / sensitive; sensitive execution profile. This bounded verifier, regression, and documentation change should fit the 16-hour claim budget. Require independent security review of actor provenance, permission response interpretation, and all operation admissions before implementation acceptance.

## What we know

- `internal/tracker/github.go:98` (`VerifyForkRepository`) rejects any slug whose owner differs from the supplied actor, checks `fork` and `source.full_name`, and optionally checks token-relative repository permissions. This owner equality blocks organization forks; removing it alone would grant excess authority.
- `internal/cli/root.go:217` (`verifyForkRemote`) gets the logged-in identity with `CurrentUser` and calls the verifier with `requirePush=true`. `internal/fork/coordinator.go:109` calls the same verifier with the API-verified event actor and `requirePush=false`; coordinator-token permissions cannot establish that actor's rights.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:119` verifies event/comment provenance. `executeRequest` at line 266 authorizes `acquire`, `acquire-pr`, and all remaining mutations through the shared fork verifier (lines 311, 330, 358). Remaining mutations first enforce active claim ID, owner, and expiry. Authoritative state supplies the fork after acquisition.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:622` verifies linked PR head repository, branch and upstream; completion separately checks revision evidence. Preserve these checks and expected-head comparisons.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:185` already uses GitHub's exact-repository collaborator permission endpoint for upstream authorization. Fork authorization needs a separate use of that API, never a call granting upstream maintainer rights.
- Existing coverage: `TestForkGitHubTrackerVerifyForkAndGetPullRequest` (`internal/tracker/github_test.go:427`), `TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle` (`internal/fork/fork_test.go:291`), CLI remote fixtures (`internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:228`), and PR contributor workflows (`internal/pr/service_test.go:605`, `:802`). `internal/fork/operations_test.go:16` guards operation-list synchronization.
- `docs/fork-mode.md:5`, `:127`, `:130` and CLI help (`internal/cli/root.go:116`, `:197`) describe personal forks only. SECURITY.md's PR-revision boundary says the coordinator verifies fork ownership; this needs a narrow clarification.

## What we're assuming

- GitHub's collaborator permission response can establish effective write/maintain/admin access for the named actor on an accessible organization fork. Fake REST fixtures will verify parsing and exact request targeting; actual GitHub visibility/policy behavior belongs to PR review.
- The provided detached source is the approved snapshot. Git metadata is unavailable (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails); the coordinator/developer must confirm against approved base before implementation. No new Go files are needed. Proposed `changes/unreleased/284.md` is absent in the snapshot; verify absence at approved base before creating it, otherwise modify the existing fragment.

## Open questions

- Which private-fork permission lookups can the deployed coordinator read? Fail closed for unavailable evidence and document access/setup requirements. The optional live review matrix answers deployment compatibility, without blocking fake-client implementation or requesting agent credentials.
- Does GitHub return effective standard permission for custom organization roles? Accept only explicit standard write-capable permission evidence; unknown/missing values fail closed. Do not infer capability from a custom role name. Cover this in parser tests and independent review.

## Implementation sequence and exact touchpoints

1. Modify `internal/tracker/github.go:98`, retaining `VerifyForkRepository` as the shared policy entry point. Rename the semantic parameter from expected owner to actor (including injection parameter names in `internal/cli/root.go:49` and `internal/fork/coordinator.go:83`). Reject empty actors. Fetch repository metadata and validate canonical full name/owner/name consistency against the requested slug, fork status, and exact upstream source. Reject contradictory metadata instead of authorizing a different returned repository. Compare GitHub identities case-insensitively; escape each URL component.
2. Preserve personal-fork behavior: API owner equals actor, plus existing token push check for CLI discovery. A different personal owner stays denied. For a different owner, require API owner type `Organization` and fresh `GET repos/<canonical-owner>/<canonical-repo>/collaborators/<verified-actor>/permission`. Accept explicit `write`, `maintain`, or `admin`; reject read/triage/none, missing/unknown evidence, errors, and cancellation. Do this even when `requirePush=false`. Repository `permissions.push/admin`, organization membership, request fields, and coordinator identity never substitute. Preserve the CLI token push check as an additional check when requested. Do not cache permission decisions across operations.
3. Keep `Coordinator.verifyForkRepo` and CLI `verifyForkRemote` routed through this verifier. Audit all cases in `executeRequest` against `fork.Operations`: acquire uses the request slug only after API verification; acquire-pr and all later operations use the authoritative recorded fork. Recheck organization permissions on every operation, including renew/release, artifacts, checkpoints, submission, begin/record/invalidate/rebase/complete PR revision. Preserve event identity, claims/index ownership by actor, replay checks, CAS fences, approvals, ancestry, exact PR linkage and expected remote heads. No new operations, state formats, bypass flags, workflow or protected-file changes.
4. Extend existing fake REST and local Git fixture tests in `internal/tracker/github_test.go`, `internal/fork/fork_test.go`, `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go`, and `internal/pr/service_test.go`. Use the same actor login for personal and organization cases. Coordinator tests must exercise the real tracker verifier with fake HTTP responses, not merely an always-successful `VerifyForkFunc`. Include a table over every operation with denied/revoked permission, and assert no authoritative mutation; retain operation-list synchronization coverage. See TEST_PLAN.md for adversarial cases.
5. Update `docs/fork-mode.md` introduction, remote setup, security and PR revision wording for an actor-owned personal fork or an organization fork with verified actor write access. Explain GitHub private-fork creation/visibility policy and coordinator permission-evidence access with actionable administrator setup guidance; inaccessible evidence stops the operation. Use existing flags only. Update CLI help/remedy in `internal/cli/root.go` to say contributor fork. Narrowly update SECURITY.md's PR-revision bullet to distinguish verified actor write permission on an organization fork from personal ownership, while preserving claim and maintainer approval requirements. Add `changes/unreleased/284.md` following existing fragment style.
6. Run focused tests, approved checks, and make check. Have an independent reviewer examine authorization response binding and operation coverage. Put the optional live public/private × personal/organization matrix in the eventual PR review checklist, using one logged-in account; never require live credentials in agent acceptance.

## HANDOFF

- Entry points: tracker verifier `internal/tracker/github.go:98`; CLI discovery `internal/cli/root.go:217`; coordinator wrapper `internal/fork/coordinator.go:109`, admissions `:266`, PR linkage `:622`. Source references are starting points to verify, not authority over approved inputs or gates.
- Extend fixtures/tests listed above; preserve `internal/fork/operations_test.go:16` and existing personal lifecycle/adversarial coverage. Focused commands: `go test ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/lease`; `go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/lease`.
- Checked assumptions: both discovery and coordinator call the same verifier (source inspection); all coordinator mutation groups already pass its wrapper (switch inspection); personal-only docs/help found by repository search. Source has no Git metadata, so approved-base fragment absence remains a developer check.
- Reopen the plan if effective actor permissions cannot be verified with the available GitHub API, if implementing requires new credentials/users, protected workflow changes, upstream authority changes, or local state migration. Fail closed and report the gap instead of widening scope.
- **What this change breaks:** tracker tests expecting all differing owners to fail must distinguish organization owner type plus actor permission from unrelated personal owners; preserve the latter rejection. The coordinator-without-token-push personal test remains valid. CLI fake metadata/permission fixtures must add organization responses without changing personal behavior. PR tests relying on actor login as head owner must parameterize fork owner separately while retaining actor claim ownership. Personal-only CLI help, docs/fork-mode.md and SECURITY.md ownership wording receive the narrow updates above. `VerifyForkFunc`/`forkVerifyFunc` signatures remain compatible, but parameter meaning becomes actor. Transport schemas, fork operations, workflow admission lists, lease state formats, upstream authorization and approval tests stay unchanged.

<!-- swarm:guidance:start -->
## Operator guidance

> The operator wants both personal and organization-owned forks tested using the same logged-in account. Plan verified write authorization for the exact actor on the exact fork, never inferring authority from organization membership or coordinator-token permissions. Preserve lineage, claim fences, upstream approval and expected-head checks across issue and PR operations. Inspect SECURITY.md and include a narrow clarification if its current personal-fork wording needs updating. No live GitHub credentials in agent acceptance; use fake client adversarial tests. Stop after planning.

# ISSUE-284 test plan

All automated acceptance uses fake GitHub REST clients and temporary local Git repositories. No live credentials, network service, or extra account is required. New regressions must demonstrate failure against the old organization-owner rejection or missing actor-specific authorization behavior.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC1: authorized organization forks support personal issue and PR workflows, exact lineage, public/accessibly private discovery and admission | In tracker and CLI fixture tables use the same `alice` login with `alice/swarm` and `builders/swarm`; set public/private metadata independently. Organization API owner type is Organization; actor permission write/maintain/admin permits discovery and real-verifier coordinator admission. Assert exact collaborator URL names alice and builders/swarm, even when coordinator identity differs. Exercise issue acquire/checkpoint/submission and PR acquire/work/rebase/checkpoint/completion with separate actor and fork owner. Assert canonical fork, actor-owned claim/index, linked PR and validated head. Preserve personal tests. |
| AC2: adversarial rejection and preserved fences | Reject read/triage/none organization members, unrelated actor without permission, other personal owner, missing/unknown owner type for organization admission, forged event/comment/request authority, inconsistent returned slug/owner/name, nonfork, wrong/missing upstream source. Reject permission 403/404/5xx, malformed/missing/unknown permission, canceled request, and permission revoked after acquisition. Token push/admin true with actor read must fail; actor write with CLI token push false must still fail discovery. On denial assert state revision, replay marker, lease, artifacts and contributor index unchanged. Preserve stale/expired/successor claim, changed head, ancestry, unapproved plan and validation-head mismatch rejection in organization workflows. |
| AC3: one rule across every operation, docs and full checks | Drive the operation list through valid existing fixture preconditions, deny/revoke organization permission for each admission and assert the verifier is consulted and no mutation occurs; success representatives cover issue and all PR revision/rebase transitions. Keep TestOperationListsStayInSync passing. Inspect docs/help/security wording and private-fork setup; run focused and full checks below. |

Extend `TestForkGitHubTrackerVerifyForkAndGetPullRequest`, `TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle` (both ledger namespaces), `TestUpstreamRemoteForkFlow`, `TestForkRemoteDefaults`, `TestForkContributorRevisesOwnPR`, and `TestForkContributorResolvesRebaseConflictsAsReports`. Add table-driven cases in their existing files; no production-only mock authorization shortcuts. Distinguish expected authorization denial from unrelated fixture failures with endpoint-call assertions and error checks. Ensure permission freshness by changing the fake response between successful acquire and subsequent mutation. For stale claims preserve errors.Is(..., lease.ErrClaimFence); test changed heads with otherwise valid organization permissions so the head checks themselves are reached.

Run from repository root during implementation:

```bash
go test ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/lease
go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli ./internal/pr ./internal/lease
make check
go build ./...
go test ./...
```

Also run the approved formatting check (`gofmt -s -l .`, requiring empty output), `go vet ./...`, and `go tool staticcheck ./...`; make check includes vet, staticcheck and race coverage. Run make fmt during implementation before checks. Validate changed Markdown relative links/anchors and any modified bash snippets with `bash -n`; confirm documented CLI options against Cobra registrations. Review fragment format against changes/unreleased examples. Independent security review must confirm exact actor/exact fork API evidence and all operation paths, not just successful tests.

PR review checklist only: using the same logged-in contributor account, try public personal, public organization, accessible-private personal, and accessible-private organization forks for issue and PR revision/rebase workflows. Record GitHub policy or permission-evidence access limitations and actionable setup; inaccessible private forks must fail closed. This live matrix is outside automated acceptance and does not block implementation in the sandbox.

Planning validation: confirm both artifacts cover all three criteria and touch no production/protected files. Implementation tests have not been run during this planning-only phase.
